cards.explanation: The answer is that we keep His commandments. The writer says, "By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments." Knowing Him shows up in how we live, friends. It's not just something we say.

The answer is liar. The writer doesn't sugarcoat it: "…he is a liar, and the truth is not in him." Those are strong words, friends. They match verse 3, where knowing Him and keeping His commandments go together.

The answer is as Jesus walked. The writer says whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked. Jesus Himself is the pattern, friends. It's like pressing from the original stamp instead of a blurry copy, and the original is what I want my cookies coming from.

The answer is True. The writer says, "Beloved, I am not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one, which you have had from the beginning." Then he adds that this commandment is the message you have heard. They'd had it all along, friends.

The answer is that the darkness is fading and the light is shining. The writer says, "For the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining." Fading means it's on its way out, and already shining means the light is here now. It's like the kitchen at sunrise, with the dark backing out as the light comes in.

The answer is False. The writer says that someone who claims to be in the light but hates his brother "…is still in the darkness." Still in it, he says, friends. Saying you're in the light isn't the same as being in it.

The answer is in the light. The writer says, "Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him." That's the other side of verse 9, friends. Loving his brother and living in the light go together.

The answer is that the darkness has blinded his eyes. The writer says he does not know where he is going, "…because the darkness has blinded his eyes." I think this one is heavy, friends. It's a sad picture of someone walking with no sight, and the writer says it plainly.

The answer is forgiven! The writer says he writes to the little children "…because your sins have been forgiven through His name." Forgiven means the sins are dealt with, and it's through His name. That's good news worth writing down, friends.
The answer is True. The writer says, "I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning." He says it again in verse 14. The fathers are the ones who know Him, friends.
The answer is the evil one. The writer says, "I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one." The young men have won that one, friends. He says it again in verse 14.

The answer is strong! The writer tells the young men, "…you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one." Strong and the word of God abiding in them go side by side, friends. That's quite a list.

The answer is the love of the Father. The writer says, "If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him." He doesn't dress it up, friends. Loving the world and the love of the Father don't sit in the same heart.
The answer is False. The writer says the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes and the pride of life are "…not from the Father but from the world." They come from the world, friends.

The answer is whoever does the will of God. The writer says, "…whoever does the will of God remains forever." The world is passing away, but the one who does God's will remains, friends. That's the long view.
